articles.excerpt: The Ignite Fire Festival in Rochdale will showcase a stunning trail of fire and light this November, promising an exciting family-friendly experience.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale is set to host the Ignite Fire Festival this November, transforming the town with a spectacular display of fire, lights, and sound.

Organised by the Rochdale Development Agency, the festival aims to create a festive atmosphere leading up to Christmas, featuring new attractions including blazing fire sculptures and illuminated installations.

The festival will centre around an immersive night-time trail titled 'BODY,' which will take visitors on an educational journey through the human body.

This multi-sensory experience will be executed using cutting-edge technology, promising to be the most ambitious light display yet, led by the renowned outdoor art company, Walk the Plank.

The gardens and square surrounding Rochdale Town Hall, along with the parkland on Broadfield slopes, will be transformed into a vibrant vision of festive light and colour. The Fire Garden will showcase intricate, hand-crafted fire sculptures, enhancing the visual spectacle of the event.

The Ignite Fire Festival is a free, family-friendly event, making it an excellent opportunity for local families to enjoy a festive evening together. As the town prepares for the holiday season, this event is expected to draw significant attendance, contributing to the community's festive spirit.

articles.excerpt: Nine men have been convicted for their roles in a child sex grooming ring in Rochdale, abusing vulnerable girls between 2008 and 2010.
articles.content_html:

The victims, some of whom were runaways or in the care of social services, were groomed with attention and then subjected to abuse, including being plied with alcohol and raped. This case highlights the serious issue of child exploitation in the area.

The convictions were based on evidence provided by the victims, who bravely came forward to share their experiences. This case has drawn significant attention to the need for better protection and support for vulnerable children in Rochdale and beyond.

As a result of the convictions, there is an ongoing discussion about improving safeguarding measures and support systems for at-risk youth in the community. This case underscores the importance of vigilance and proactive measures to protect children from exploitation.

articles.title: Rochdale Bonfire Night celebrations set for Bowlee Community Park and Heywood
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's Bonfire Night celebrations will feature fireworks displays at three locations, starting at Bowlee Community Park on November 2.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale's Bonfire Night celebrations will kick off with a fireworks display at Bowlee Community Park in Middleton on November 2, starting at 7:30pm. The event promises a festive atmosphere with food and soft drinks available for purchase.

Following the Middleton event, a second fireworks display will take place on November 3 at Queen’s Park Road in Heywood, also beginning at 7:30pm. This event is expected to attract local families and residents looking to enjoy the Bonfire Night festivities.

The final event in the series will occur on November 4 at Cronkeyshaw Common, rounding off the celebrations with another fireworks display at the same time. Each event aims to provide a safe and enjoyable experience for attendees of all ages.

These celebrations are significant for the local community, offering a chance for families to come together and enjoy the traditional Bonfire Night festivities. Residents are encouraged to attend and participate in the celebrations.

articles.title: New transport policing command to cover Rochdale’s buses, trams and roads
articles.excerpt: A new Greater Manchester command brings transport and roads policing together, with more than 60 new officers announced across the network. No separate Rochdale allocation has been published.
articles.content_html:
People travelling on Rochdale’s buses, trams and roads will be covered by a new Greater Manchester policing command launched today, Thursday 29 October.

The Transport Policing and Crime Command brings Greater Manchester Police, Transport for Greater Manchester and the combined authority into a closer working structure to tackle crime, antisocial behaviour and dangerous driving across the transport network.

Chief Superintendent Suzanne Downey leads the command, which police describe as an effective 11th policing district alongside the region’s ten borough districts. The announcement includes more than 60 new officers across the network. It does not give a separate allocation for Rochdale or say how many additional patrols individual stops and routes will receive.

The command also incorporates the existing Roads Policing Unit, including specialist teams that investigate serious collisions and deal with commercial vehicles and motorcycle policing. New recruits are to be funded through additional mayoral investment, which police say will protect existing frontline resources.

Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said: “TPACC represents a significant step forward in how we police and protect Greater Manchester's transport network.”

For Rochdale passengers, the practical question is whether closer coordination produces a more visible presence and quicker responses on the journeys they use. The announcement sets out those aims, rather than evidence that they have already been achieved.

The command’s roads teams have already operated in the borough. In a separate statement published on 3 September, police described stopping vehicles in Rochdale after reports of dangerous driving on the M66 and M62. That earlier operation is separate from today’s formal launch.

The new structure will work alongside TravelSafe LiveChat, which allows passengers to report concerns discreetly through the Bee Network app or QR codes on buses and trams. According to the launch release, more than 2,000 reports have been made through the service, with police responding to 800 incidents. Those are network-wide figures, not Rochdale totals.

Control room staff at police and TfGM will support the command using CCTV across the transport system. The plans also support Greater Manchester’s stated ambition to eliminate deaths and serious injuries on its roads by 2040.

Source: Greater Manchester Police’s launch release, supplied on 28 October under an embargo that expired at 6am on 29 October, and its published report of the September roads operation. No borough-specific staffing or incident figures were supplied.

articles.title: Rochdale Diversity Awards celebrate community contributions
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Diversity Awards, held on October 28, 2026, recognised individuals and organisations making a positive impact in the community, with MP Paul Waugh in attendance.
articles.content_html:
The Rochdale Diversity Awards took place on October 28, 2026, celebrating individuals and organisations that have made significant contributions to equality and community cohesion in Rochdale.

The event, organised by KYP since 2012, highlighted inspiring stories of local heroes who have worked to break down barriers and strengthen community ties.

Zulf Ahmed, a prominent figure in the community, described the awards as incredibly special, emphasising the importance of recognising those who help others thrive. The ceremony brought together community leaders and members, showcasing the best of Rochdale's efforts to promote diversity and inclusion.

Among the attendees was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who supported the initiative aimed at fostering a fairer and more inclusive environment in the borough. The awards not only acknowledge individual achievements but also aim to inspire others to contribute positively to the community.

The event is part of a broader initiative to promote diversity in Rochdale, encouraging ongoing efforts to create a more cohesive society. The next steps involve continuing to support and highlight the work of those dedicated to making a difference in the community.

Delivered by KYP (Kashmir Youth Project) since 2012, the awards recognised outstanding contributions to equality, diversity, inclusion and community cohesion. With finalists selected from more than 130 nominations, the evening showcased the very best of Rochdale and the people whose efforts make a positive difference every day. The evening brought together civic leaders, businesses, public sector organisations, charities, community groups and residents to celebrate the people and organisations whose dedication continues to break down barriers, create opportunities and strengthen communities. Zulf Ahmed, Chief Executive Officer of KYP, said: “The Rochdale Diversity Awards are about recognising the people and organisations whose commitment, compassion and leadership make a real difference to others every day. “This year we received more than 130 nominations, each telling a story of someone breaking down barriers, creating opportunities or helping others to thrive. Bringing together more than 350 guests to celebrate those achievements was incredibly special. Rochdale MP Paul Waugh with some of the winners. Image: Paul Waugh “The awards remind us of the strength of our communities and the extraordinary things that happen when people come together with a shared commitment to making Rochdale a fairer, more inclusive and more connected borough.” The audience also heard inspiring contributions from civic and community leaders from across the borough. Cllr Andy Kelly, Deputy Mayor of Rochdale, spoke of his pride in Rochdale’s diverse communities and reflected on how the borough’s rich mix of cultures, backgrounds and traditions continues to be one of its greatest strengths. Cllr Neil Emmott, Leader of Rochdale Borough Council, highlighted the importance of partnership and collective action in tackling inequality, strengthening communities and creating opportunities for residents across the borough. Elsie Blundell MP, Member of Parliament for Heywood and Middleton North, praised the generosity, resilience and community spirit she has witnessed across Rochdale, highlighting the importance of bringing people together, breaking down barriers and creating opportunities for everyone to succeed. READ MORE: New industrial units could inspire town’s entrepreneurs Julie Murphy, Chief Executive of Rochdale Council, said: “A truly inclusive community is one where nobody feels they have to leave part of themselves at the door to be accepted. We want every child and young person to believe they can succeed, regardless of their background or circumstances. “The finalists and winners we celebrate tonight are a powerful example of what can be achieved when we break down barriers, embrace diversity and create opportunities for everyone to thrive.” Paul Waugh MP, Member of Parliament for Rochdale and Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Early Education, said: “The people and organisations recognised tonight represent the very best of Rochdale. “Their dedication, compassion and commitment to helping others demonstrate the strength of our communities and the values that bring us together as a borough.” Mohammed (Attaur) Rahman, founder of Rochdale Science Initiative CIC, winner of the Breaking Barriers Award and Outstanding Achievement in Diversity Award, said: “Celebrating at the Rochdale Diversity Awards was a powerful reminder of what makes our borough special: its people, their resilience and their commitment to helping others thrive. Heywood and Middleton North MP Elsie Blundell with guests at the awards “These awards recognise the collective efforts of volunteers, community organisations and partners who work every day to create opportunities and remove barriers. It is an honour to be recognised alongside so many individuals and organisations making a meaningful difference across Rochdale.” Entertainment was provided by the K&K Queensway Royals Morris Dancing Troupe, which opened the evening with a vibrant performance reflecting the rich diversity and cultural heritage celebrated throughout the awards. The event was made possible through the generous support of Rochdale Boroughwide Housing, Altus Education Partnership, Rochdale Council, Your Trust, Hopwood Hall College, For Generations to Come, Ingeus, Harvest Touch Youth & Skills Community Hub, Greater Manchester High Sheriff’s Police Trust, Action Together and Rochdale Development Agency. The Rochdale Diversity Awards 2026 supported support Springhill Hospice as the event’s charity partner. Their dedication to providing outstanding care and support to patients and families across our communities reflects the values of compassion and service celebrated throughout the evening. The Rochdale Diversity Awards continue to recognise the individuals, community groups, employers, public services and voluntary organisations whose work strengthens communities, creates opportunities and helps make Rochdale a more inclusive borough. As planning begins for 2027, the awards remain an important celebration of the people whose efforts make a lasting difference to the lives of others across Rochdale. articles.title: Lachlan Lanskey joins Rochdale Hornets on one-year deal for 2027 season
articles.excerpt: Australia-born Ireland international Lachlan Lanskey has signed with Rochdale Hornets for the upcoming season after leaving Keighley Cougars.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Hornets have confirmed the signing of Lachlan Lanskey on a one-year deal for the 2027 season. The Australia-born Ireland international joins the club following his departure from Keighley Cougars, where he played for three years.

Lanskey, a back-rower, is a product of the Brisbane Broncos’ youth system and has represented Queensland at various youth levels.

Although he did not make an NRL appearance, he played for Brisbane Tigers in the Queensland Cup before moving to the UK in 2023 to join Whitehaven.

Currently, Lanskey represents Ireland internationally, having made his debut last autumn in a Test Series against Wales. He recently starred in a match against Scotland in the Celtic Cup, marking his third cap for the Wolfhounds.

Expressing his excitement about the move, Lanskey stated, “I’m really happy to be getting on board for the 2027 season.” His addition is expected to bolster Rochdale's squad as they prepare for the upcoming Championship campaign.
